verdict.rationale: Linear ships a built-in Linear Agent that users can hand work to. It can write code via Claude Code and Codex, set up, run and test code before returning it, and investigate and attempt fixes on new issues. Delegated issues get their own section showing coding-session status, Loops let the agent take on recurring work, and Write with Agent drafts updates. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the built-in agent's delegation quality, since all evidence is vendor changelog claims.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Linear Agent can now write code using Claude Code and Codex. You can triage, plan, review, and ship—all in Linear.
Linear Agent can now set up, run, and test your code before returning its work.
When a new issue is reported, Linear Agent can investigate and attempt a fix before it reaches an engineer, reducing the load on your team.
We’ve also added section under My Issues → Assigned for your delegated issues. It shows the status of each coding session, and gives you a quick way back into active work.
Loops are a new way for Linear Agent to take on recurring work for your team. Describe the job in plain language and then choose whether it should run on a schedule or in response to an event.
Instead of finding that context manually, click Write with Agent to let Linear do it for you.
